summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (95/231)

data.turoyo: Əmmi, qrelela l Teli ʕAyšane, məlle: “Samiwayno, hani tloṯo yawme, tloṯo lalye ṭaʕino u lġono b feme d Beǧaġa Baye, azze ḥayat diḏi mi arʕo, gqoṭeli ʕAli Aġa.”
data.translation: Da rief er Teli Aischane und sprach: Ich bin blind gewesen Drei Tage und drei Nächte habe ich das Gebiss im Maule von Bedschagha Bae vergessen. Nun ist es um mein Leben geschehen, Ali Agha wird mich töten.

rationale: First Preterit-wa box and figurative sense 2 in an anterior neglected-duty context.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.22/1150)

data.turoyo: Əno ḥoṯi i Nəǧo samənwo ʕayna mərlən: “Kito toxtor Matta b Mawṣal.“
data.translation: My sister Nejo, her eyes had become blind; they told us, “There is Doctor Matta in Mosul.”

rationale: First literal I.1 Preterit-wa cell; round 1 added that box only for figurative I.2.

summary: New sense 2: fig. verblendet sein, aus Unverstand handeln

data.gloss: fig. verblendet sein, aus Unverstand handeln

rationale: Three self-reproaches concern an unwise choice or neglected situation, without a physical loss of sight; the first-person sami/samyo and -wa forms support grouping the figurative use.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (PrS 34/93)

data.turoyo: Ummi: "Qay smiṯo hat?" Ummo: "Ḥəngi d baxyono, samyono." Ummo: "Gmanəḥono ʕaynəx." - Nure.
data.translation: »Wie kommt es denn, dass du blind bist?« fragten sie. »Weil ich so viel geweint habe, bin ich blind«, erwiderte sie. Da sagte Nûre: »Ich will deine Augen heilen«.

rationale: Unusual first-person feminine Preterit Intransitive contrasts with lexical smiṯo in the same sentence; clearer than a third-person homophonous adjective.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (57/11)

data.translation: Ich bin blind geworden, ich kann nichts vor mir sehen.

rationale: Distinct first-person masculine result assertion and explicit present inability to see.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 10/57)

data.turoyo: somən ʕayne d emux, mḏ̣ayəʕ aḥunux.
data.translation: die Augen deiner Mutter mögen blind werden; dein Bruder ist verschwunden!

rationale: Infectum has three existing examples; optative with eyes as subject and complete lament.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (115/183)

data.turoyo: Aḥna xəlṣina, u faqirawo d Baṣuṣ gəzze, gsome hənge, gboxe tamo, zan, dəʕrinale!
data.translation: Sollen wir gerettet werden, und der arme Basus oben soll sich blind weinen? Laß uns zu ihm zurückkehren!

rationale: Second addition to the thin Infectum cell: prospective g- and crying context.

rationale: New figurative sense 2; self-reproach linked to the wrong sword recipient. Edition quote is limited to the figurative predicate.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 4.5/18)

data.turoyo: mḥalaqqe bəṯrayye, ba ayko kḥuzanne, Aloho gəmasmelən
data.translation: Sie nahmen die Verfolgung auf, doch wo wollten sie sie sehen, Gott machte sie blind.

rationale: Sparse stem-III Infectum cell: overt causer plus plural indexed patient; narrative use of gə-.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (57/8)

data.turoyo: Ṭaw me d məḥyono ruḥi ebe, b ḥḏo ḏ̣arbo masəmyalle, layt.
data.translation: Das Beste ist: ich werfe mich auf ihn und mache ihn mit einem Schlage blind.

rationale: Sparse III Infectum: first-person feminine actor, indexed patient and b- instrument.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 44/90)

data.turoyo: Masmela w mdaywalle, nošo lə kmaǧre mqadamla mu bazərgan w peva.
data.translation: aber sie machte ihn blind und verrückt, Niemand durfte sich ihr nähern ausser dem Kaufmanne ganz allein.

rationale: III Preterit has two examples; clear sequential causative blinding.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (57/26)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Aṯyo, mḥela ruḥa ebi, ač čangatayḏa b ʕayni, masmelali w fayito, azza."
data.translation: Da kam sie und warf sich auf mich, schlug mit den Flügeln auf meine Augen, machte mich blind und flog davon."

rationale: III Preterit: first-person patient encoded after feminine actor suffix; improves sparse cell.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (83/23)

data.turoyo: Ḥəffe, mlalle ʕayne masmalle mu ṣafono w ftəḥḥe u tarʕo w mḥalaqqe larwal. Tfəkke larwal mḥalaqqe. (w naḥət bi kaṣe).
data.translation: Sie wuschen ihn, machten ihm die Augen voller Seife und machten ihn damit blind. Dann öffneten sie die Tür und warfen ihn, stießen ihn hinaus. (Zuhörer: und er stürzte den Abhang hinunter).

rationale: Fifth III Preterit example: temporary blinding by soap, with m- cause.

summary: Remove the duplicated d before i=emaṯṯe
rationale: The quotation writes the genitive linker twice, once at the end of mə-gawə-d and again in d-i=emaṯṯe. The supplied 3/24 has m gawe di emaṯṯe with a single d. This removes a duplicated consonant, while retaining the glossary clitic notation.

summary: I is inchoative/resultative with the affected person or eyes as subject and no l-agent. III adds a causer, with the blinded person as bare NP or indexed patient; 57/8 contrasts the two stems in one episode.
Age, crying, physical injury, glare and soap provide causes or contexts, not separately numbered senses. Pretended blindness in 76/143-144 changes the truth of the claim, not its lexical meaning.

Infectum occurs in optatives and predictions; Preterit Intransitive often reports the resulting state. III Preterit in 57/8 is prospective within a temporal plan, so edition tense alone cannot classify the box.

The adjective samyo plus yo contrasts with inchoative k-somən, already within 3/24. A masculine samyo yo predicate is not automatically a Part act.; first-person samino/samyono can still require contextual verbal/adjectival review.
Existing unnumbered examples belong to each stem’s sole original sense 1; effective existing counts are I Preterit Intransitive 4, I Infectum 3, III Preterit 2 and III Infectum 1.
samənwo with plural eyes adds literal anterior/resultant blindness to the Preterit-wa box that round 1 proposed only for figurative self-reproach.
The optative sumeno in remorse wishes physical blindness and remains I.1; remorse does not by itself make a figurative blindness sense.
samyowa remains a verbal/adjectival boundary question already raised in round 1; machine English had gone blind does not resolve that boundary.

Confirm finite Preterit Intransitive versus adjective-plus-copula in the figurative samino/samyono self-reproaches; the figurative meaning is supported, but its morphological treatment is provisional.
Is samyo a lexical adjective throughout the copular attestations, or is there independent evidence for a productive Part act. paradigm?
Does JTM 4.5/18 denote actual supernatural loss of sight or temporary inability to notice the escapees? Keep literal causative meaning until clarified.
Is 77/175 ordinary temporary loss of vision or hyperbole? No new sense is introduced from the English paraphrase.
The supplied German at 70/200 ends with Mein Vater and lacks the final blindness assertion; obtain the matching edition continuation before quoting it.
Is samyowa at Jan 1.31/1378 a finite feminine Preterit-wa or a blind-state adjective with past copula? No added finite example is based on it.
Use the plural stones after these
rationale: These requires the plural stones. The Turoyo ak=kef-anək and the corpus bak kefanək also refer to plural stones. Preserve the editorial addition (precious).

summary: Eyes as subjects and temporary dazzling/soap obstruction retain loss-of-vision meaning; no independent dazzle sense.
Causation includes divine intervention and temporary soap-induced inability to see; no change in causative valency or a separate supernatural sense.
